magnetDesc.message: When the search term is 40 alphanumeric characters, or you paste such a string in the popup, magnet:?xt=urn:btih: is prefixed and the link is opened. When disabled this feature does not take effect.

baiduDesc.message: When the search term is 28 characters of letters / digits / hyphen (with a hyphen at the 5th position from the end and 4 alphanumeric characters after it), or you paste such a string in the popup, it is prefixed with https://pan.baidu.com/s/ and the - is replaced by ?pwd=. When disabled this feature does not take effect.

addressBarDesc.message:
Enable address bar search.
It intercepts traffic to the configured address, checks whether the search term is a magnet / Baidu Pan link, and falls back to your custom search engine when nothing matches.

interceptDesc.message:
The address template intercepted by the extension. Visiting an address in this template format will be intercepted: magnet / Pan links are redirected directly, everything else is sent to your browser's default search engine.
It can also serve as a browser search shortcut — click the link above to copy the default template and set it as your default search engine. You can then paste a magnet hash or Pan link straight into the address bar while normal queries still go to search.
Once the address is set as your default search engine, you can change the intercepted address here. Any valid URL format works, even a non-existent site.
Note: after changing the address here you must set the new template as your browser's default search engine again for it to take effect.
Use $$s for the position of the search term.

guideTitle.message: How to set as the default search engine ($BROWSER$)

guideChromeSteps.message:
• Under "Site search", click "Add"
  • Paste the copied address into the "URL" field ($$s has been converted to the required %s and autolinkdefault=true appended)
  • Fill in any "Name" / "Shortcut", then save
  • Click the "⋮" next to the entry → "Make default"

guideEdgeSteps.message:
• Click "Add search engine"
  • Paste the copied address into "URL (use %s in place of the search term)" (autolinkdefault=true is already appended)
  • Fill in any "Name" / "Shortcut", then click "Add"
  • Find the newly added engine at the bottom of the list and click "⋮" → "Make default"

guideOperaSteps.message:
• Under "Search engines", click "Add"
  • Paste the copied address into "URL"
  • Save, then click "Make default"

guideFirefoxSteps.message:
• Open $URL$
  • Firefox does not support adding a custom search engine by pasting a URL; an OpenSearch description file is required
  • If you need this feature, consider Chrome or Edge

guideOtherSteps.message:
• Open your browser's search engine settings
  • Add a new search engine and paste the copied address into "URL"
  • Set it as the default
